summary: starlette-healthchecks exfiltrates environment variable names and host identifiers to hardcoded Azure endpoint
details: The package exposes configure_logging() which, on default invocation, spawns a background thread that iterates os.environ and POSTs every environment variable name (values masked) along with a masked hostname tail and the last octet of the machine's public IP to the hardcoded endpoint ca-fusion-dev-collector.mangoriver-32d7264e.uksouth.azurecontainerapps.io. The destination host and API key (`fusion-default-api-key`) are baked into the code as defaults, and the endpoint is on a generic azurecontainerapps.io subdomain unrelated to the package's declared publisher. The package name suggests a healthcheck library while the actual behavior is bulk enumeration of installer environment variable names to an author-controlled collector. Enumerating environment variable names reveals which secrets and services the installer uses (AWS_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, DB_*, CI-specific variables), even when values are masked.
